newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee extends bull run, highest since Oct 94.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee extends bull run, highest since Oct 94.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures raced to their highest level in nearly two and a half years on Wednesday, sailing through the widely-watched $2 a lb mark, despite a late-session round of profit-taking, dealers said.

In yet another hectic session for the coffee market, roaster buying sent prices sharply higher from the opening bell. Speculators joined the buying spree, driving the benchmark May contract up 14.25 cents at one point.
As the market neared the 210.00 cent barrier, however, a wave of profit-taking erased the bulk of the gains.

At the close, May ended up 5.40 cents per lb, at 200.65 cents. March rose 8.10, to 219.75. May futures traded as high as 209.50 cents per lb, up seven percent from the previous close and the highest level since October, 1994.

A move by the CSCE to raise deposit margins on the spot March contract by $2,000 to $7,000 helped fuel the run-up, said Victor Henriquez, managing director of Hencorp Becstone, a coffee trading firm in Miami.
"Margin calls are very high for the shorts, so you had a lot of short-covering," he said. Margins on the spot month have risen by $5,250 since the start of the year.
"There is a lack of sellers because everyone who wanted to sell the market already sold it," Henriquez said. "As long as there is no coffee coming into the market, no one can stop it."
After rising 30 cents, or 17 percent, in four days, today's reversal near the 210.00 cent mark may signal a short-term top for the market, but traders said any pullback was likely to be short-lived.
"It's possible that the market could come in a little lower tomorrow, but I wouldn't look for a big correction by any means," a trader said.
Volume on the exchange was heavy, at an estimated 19,063 lots, versus Tuesday's official total of 16,060.

Technically, traders eyed a narrow chart gap created at today's open at 195.25-196. Further support was seen in the low 180s and at 177. To the upside, May would need to clear 210 to sustain the uptrend, with a longer-term objective at 225.25. ((-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
